key_insight: In rotating turbulence, large-scale geostrophic vortices are sustained by inertial-wave Reynolds stresses, and their growth depends on selective wave reflection and absorption that favors one vortex sign over the other.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict when strong rotation will amplify or suppress large-scale coherent vortices in geophysical and rotating-fluid systems, informing models of turbulence transport and momentum redistribution.
method: Direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence
Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes balance analysis for the large-scale flow
Inertial-wave field analysis to identify reflection, critical layers, and viscous absorption
evidence_signal: The abstract reports DNS evidence that wave-generated Reynolds stresses match the large-scale RANS balance and reproduce cyclone-anticyclone asymmetry, with geostrophic energy varying non-monotonically with rotation rate.
watch_item: The mechanism depends on resonant wave absorption, so predictions may change if the flow conditions or numerical resolution alter wave–vortex interactions or dissipation pathways.
paper_title: Wave-driven geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence
